questions.question: Compare RIST and RAST based on their purpose and detection.
questions.solution_html:
• Compare RIST and RAST based on their purpose and detection.
  • - RIST detects total serum IgE - RAST detects allergen-specific IgE - Both are used in
  • allergy diagnosis - RIST measures total IgE concentration - RAST identifies IgE against a
  • specific allergen
questions.final_answer: specific allergen
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain how activated B cells differentiate into antibody-secreting plasma cells.
questions.solution_html:
• - B cells recognise specific antigens - Antigen activates B cells, usually with helper T-cell
  • support - Activated B cells undergo clonal proliferation - B cells differentiate into
  • plasma cells - Plasma cells secrete specific antibodies
questions.final_answer: plasma cells - Plasma cells secrete specific antibodies
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the steps involved in indirect ELISA.
questions.solution_html:
• - Antigen is coated onto the microtitre plate - Patient serum is added - Enzyme-linked
  • secondary antibody is added - Substrate is added - Colour development indicates the
  • presence of specific antibodies
questions.final_answer: presence of specific antibodies
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: What are the major features of acquired immunity?
questions.solution_html:
• - Antigen specificity - Diversity - Immunological memory - Self/non-self
  • discrimination - Clonal expansion of specific lymphocytes
questions.final_answer: - Antigen specificity - Diversity - Immunological memory - Self/non-self
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Describe the two stages involved in complement fixation test.
questions.solution_html:
• - Stage 1: Patient serum is mixed with known antigen and complement - If specific
  • antibodies are present, antigen–antibody complexes fix the complement - Stage 2
  • Sensitised sheep red blood cells are added as an indicator system - No haemolysis
  • indicates a positive test; haemolysis indicates a negative test
questions.final_answer: indicates a positive test; haemolysis indicates a negative test
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: What are adjuvants, and explain the mechanism of immune stimulation by adjuvants.
questions.solution_html:
• • Definition of adjuvants . Examples: Alum, Freund’s adjuvant . Enhance antigen uptake
  • by antigen-presenting cells . Stimulate innate immune responses and cytokine production
  • . Improve lymphocyte activation and antibody production
questions.final_answer: . Improve lymphocyte activation and antibody production
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the primary and secondary immune responses with suitable diagrams.
questions.solution_html:
• • Definition of primary immune response . Definition of secondary immune response .
  • Primary response: slow, longer lag period and lower antibody level . Secondary response
  • rapid, higher antibody level and longer duration . Suitable labelled diagrams showing
  • antibody response over time
questions.final_answer: antibody response over time
